title: Adaptive window degeneration scratchpad
content:
Notes to self - quick log of experiments + hypotheses for the weird steady-state throughput drop after rolling batching heuristics.

TL;DR: After the adaptive window change in runtime (merge r1824) some pods show a slow throughput degeneration over ~30-90 minutes: overall qps drops ~15-35% while median latency stays ok but p95/p99 climbs. Suspect: window shrink/expand oscillation interacts poorly with prefill / KV cache eviction when request size distribution has a heavy tail (few long seqs).

Observed behavior (recap):
- On baseline canary (old heuristic) stable qps ~1200rps, p99 ~220ms.
- New heuristic: start at ~1250rps but degrades to ~800-1000rps over ~1 hour.
- CPU on inference workers: small increase (5-12%), GPU utilization unchanged.
- slot allocation traces show frequent prefill evictions after 20-40k requests per pod.
- warmup logs contain warnings: "prefill-window-too-small: eviction_count=84" on one host.

Commands I ran (fast reproducible):
- Tail batcher pod logs:
  kubectl -n inference logs deploy/rt-batcher-canary -c batcher --since=2h | grep -i eviction | tail -n 200
  => repeated: "INFO prefill: evicting prefix, slots_freed=2, eviction_reason=window_shrink"

- Dumped slot occupancy over time:
  python tools/slot_dump.py --pod rt-worker-5 --duration 3600 --out /tmp/slot-occupancy.csv
  sample output (abridged):
  ts,occupied_slots,total_slots,avg_seq_len
  00:12:00,24,32,64
  00:25:00,19,32,272   <-- spike in avg_seq_len correlated with eviction bursts
  00:42:00,14,32,68

- Quick reproduce curl through api-gateway to hit long-tail:
  for i in `seq 1 400`; do curl -s -X POST internal-api/seq-gen -d @long_prompt.json >/dev/null & done
  Monitor qps afterwards in grafana (inference.service.qps)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Adaptive window shrink when a long request arrives causes immediate eviction of prefix cache (prefill), increasing work per token for subsequent short requests. Oscillation: after eviction, window expands back and tries to re-prefill, but prefill rate lags demand so measured throughput suffers.
2) Batch packing interaction: the new window moves request boundaries so continuous-batcher forms more heterogeneous batches (mix of long and short), reducing effective batching efficiency and causing more KV cache thrash.
3) Heuristic edge case: when avg_seq_len > threshold, kernel selection switches to fallback path (less optimized) for a short time; combined with eviction this amplifies latency tail.
4) Scheduling/backpressure interplay: slot_replenish rate is not adapting to eviction frequency; leads to slot-starvation microphases.

Evidence supporting (1):
- Log correlation: eviction spikes immediately after long sequence arrivals (see slot dump).
- After artificially rate-limiting long requests, degradation stops (test with 50% riffle).

Evidence supporting (2/3):
- Batch composition: I captured batch histograms with a small script (tools/batch_hist.sh). When degraded the fraction of mixed-size batches rises from 12% -> 39%.
- CPU profiles around the time show a short bump in a fallback kernel: "kv-prefill-fallback.cpp:serve_fallback()" sampled more often.

Quick experiments and results:
- Revert adaptive-window flag for one canary ASG (rt-canary-2): immediate stabilization within 5m. qps back to ~1180. Suggests runtime heuristics directly connected.
- Added a temporary throttle on long requests in gateway (drop 1/2) -> stabilization.
- Increase prefill concurrency (prefill_workers from 2 to 4) -> partial improvement but not full recovery. Suggests filling rate matters but something else too.

Relevant snippets from logs (sanitized):

2025-01-22T00:41:12Z INFO prefill: scheduling prefill for slot=18, target_seq=64
2025-01-22T00:41:12Z WARN prefill: eviction_count=0
2025-01-22T00:45:09Z INFO prefill: evicting prefix, slots_freed=3, eviction_reason=window_shrink, active_prefills=1
2025-01-22T00:45:10Z ERROR batcher: batch_fulfillment_latency=219ms, kernel_path=fallback

Stack trace (mini) when fallback path hit: 
  serve_fallback at kv-prefill-fallback.cpp:278
  pack_batch at continuous_batcher.cpp:1421
  handle_request at rpc_worker.cpp:391

Things I want to try (next steps):
- Telemetry: emit tag on prefill-eviction events and correlate with model/kernel selection. Add metric: inference.prefill.evictions_by_reason, and batch.mixed_composition_ratio.
- Guardrail: add a soft floor on window shrink (min_window=0.5 * configured_window) to avoid catastrophic evictions from a single long request. Quick patch locally and run canary.
- Increase prefill concurrency adaptively: if eviction_rate > X per minute then bump prefill_workers; also back off once rate stabilizes.
- Change batcher packing to avoid mixing >2x length ratio in same batch (experiment).
- Add experiment: replay production long-tail arrivals into staging with full telemetry to reproduce without affecting prod.

Notes / TODO:
- Marco: please attach profiler samples for two pods (stable vs degraded) next to PR diff.
- Sofia: can you draft a short playbook blurb for SRE runbook if we see this in prod? Include rollback steps (revert flag, enable throttle).
- I should open a lightweight MTR (multi-run) comparing prefill_worker scaling strategies.

Random observations / half-formed ideas:
- Could capacitor-hysteresis (i.e., having a cooldown after eviction) smooth re-prefill bursts and avoid thrash.
- Maybe we should separate prefill KV namespace for long sequences so eviction is less disruptive to short requests (two-tier cache).

Attachment pointers I generated while testing:
- /tmp/slot-occupancy.csv (samples above)
- /tmp/batch-hist-20250122.json
- local trace: traces/rt-batcher-canary-20250122.jfr

If I had to pick a priority ordering: telemetry -> soft-floor on window shrink -> quick canary -> adaptive prefill scaling.

End notes: this is messy, but useful log of my thinking while chasing the regression. Will iterate and formalize into a playbook once we stabilize and have metrics to show.
